findings.title: FG-IR-26-170: JWT used for authentication in web GUI signed with static key (FortiMonitorOnSight, CVE-2026-84390)
findings.summary_md: Fortinet PSIRT advisory for CVE-2026-84390 (CVSSv3 9.6, CWE-540, Critical): an inclusion of sensitive information in source code in the FortiMonitorOnSight web portal, where the JWT used for GUI authentication is signed with a static key, letting a remote unauthenticated attacker bypass authentication via a forged or reused JWT. FortiMonitorOnSight 7.2.0 through 7.2.2 and 7.2.4 through 7.2.7 are affected; the fix is 7.2.8 or above. Internally discovered by Cameron Milstead of Fortinet TAC. Known Exploited: No. Timeline shows initial publication 2026-09-08, one day before the story's first_seen.

findings.title: FG-IR-26-168: Improper Authentication of FortiPAM Server (Fortinet Privileged Access Agent Chrome extension, CVE-2026-84388)
findings.summary_md: Fortinet PSIRT advisory for CVE-2026-84388 (CVSSv3 9.1, CWE-287, Critical): an improper authentication flaw in the Fortinet Privileged Access Agent Chrome extension may let a remote unauthenticated attacker proxy a user's browser traffic through attacker-controlled servers if the user visits a malicious website. FortiPAM Chrome Extension 8.0 and 7.4 all versions are affected; remediation requires FortiPAM upgraded to 1.9.1 or 1.8.4 plus the Chrome extension at 8.0.1.123 or above. Credited to Kevin Joensen (Baldur Security), Eric Brandel (Target), Dan Rosenqvist (Shelltrail), and James Arnott (Bay Area Labs). Known Exploited: No, virtual patching: No. Timeline shows initial publication 2026-09-08.

findings.title: Fortinet Privileged Access Agent: Any Site Could Control Your Proxy and Watch Your Tab
findings.summary_md: Original researcher write-up of CVE-2026-84388 by James Arnott of Bay Area Labs, covering the extension used by more than 1 million users: a webRequest listener on the path https://*/api/v2/monitor/web-ui/state added any requested hostname to the trusted-server list without checking the initiator or request success, externally_connectable was set to all URLs, non-JWT access tokens skipped validation instead of failing, and the page could click its own consent dialog (elements fortinet-sv-modal-overlay and .sv-btn-allow). Arnott states Bay Area Labs reported the issue to Fortinet on July 17 and the fix shipped August 1, and that there is no known real-world exploitation. The page displays date only (9 September 2026, no time of day); published_at is normalized to start of day UTC.
